correctness.rationale: An independent derivation gives the biased zero-level hitting recurrence, its analytic smaller root, and the exact first-return PGF. On the principal sheet the two branchpoints are the smallest singularities for p<4/5; at p=4/5 a pole collides with the positive branchpoint; above it a simple positive pole dominates. Local expansions, the branchpoint coefficient transfer and direct residue yield all constants including the parity term. Exact rational first-26 coefficients agree with a separately coded finite-time state evolution at five p values; large-n ratios support the analytic proof. Time-fixed and parameter-fixed quantifiers and the deterministic endpoint are explicit.

originality.rationale: The prior exact resetting-chain and absorption transform (Monthus 2024 eq 292) are acknowledged as input, not asserted new. Its equation 296 claims the n^-3/2 absorbing-tail form for all p>1/2 despite the divergence in the preceding sum at p>=4/5. The 4/5 rate change for a separate position correlation is already known; here the new scientific assertion is the correct three-regime first-return coefficient law, critical n^-1/2 exponent and parity constants. value.rationale: Return-time mass changes sharply at a natural dynamical parameter: below 4/5, exponential decay carries a two-parity n^-3/2 correction; at collision it has an n^-1/2 factor; above it becomes a pure pole-driven exponential. The missing regimes invalidate a previously stated uniform-in-parameter type of return/absorption asymptotic and change rare-event probabilities by unbounded polynomial factors. This is a precise natural recurrence statistic, not a selected numerical example.
